concepts.why: The presence of multiple glistening crystals in the anterior chamber, which increased in number over time, is consistent with the deposition of oxalate crystals seen in primary hyperoxaluria type 1.
The presence of a morning glory optic disc anomaly with low-lying detachment of the peripapillary retina is characteristic of morning glory syndrome.
The chronic retinal detachment observed after vitreous hemorrhage resolution is consistent with a diagnosis of retinal detachment.
The combination of oxalate crystals in the anterior chamber and chronic retinal detachment suggests a diagnosis of oxalate retinopathy.
The spontaneous hyphema and vitreous hemorrhage, followed by an increase in aqueous crystals, could be indicative of an underlying inflammatory process such as uveitis.
